content: Tigecycline is a medication used to treat certain serious bacterial infections, particularly when other antibiotics have proven ineffective. It belongs to the tetracycline class of antibiotics and is effective only against bacterial infections, not viral infections such as the common cold or flu. This medication is administered via injection into a vein over 30 to 60 minutes by a healthcare professional, typically every 12 hours as directed by your doctor. If you are using this medication at home, it is essential to learn proper preparation and administration techniques from your healthcare provider. The medication should be gently swirled to mix, not shaken, and the solution should appear yellow to orange in color. Do not use the medication if it contains particles or appears green or black. For optimal results, use this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals and complete the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, or pain and swelling at the injection site. While these effects are generally mild, it is important to remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks. If this occurs, it typically resolves after stopping the medication, but there is a risk of permanent vision loss or blindness. Tigecycline may also rarely cause a severe intestinal condition due to the bacteria Clostridium difficile (C. diff), which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after stopping the medication. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to tigecycline are rare but possible. If you experience symptoms such as rash, itching, swelling, severe dizziness, or trouble breathing, seek immediate medical attention. Before using tigecycline, inform your doctor if you are allergic to it, other tetracyclines (e.g., doxycycline, minocycline), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Additionally, tigecycline may cause dizziness, which can be worsened by alcohol or marijuana. Limit alcohol consumption while using this medication. Tigecycline may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. Children under 8 years old may be more sensitive to side effects, particularly tooth discoloration, which has also been observed in older children and young adults. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your doctor. Tigecycline should not be used during pregnancy as it may harm an unborn baby. It is unknown whether this medication passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how tigecycline works or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all medications and products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. In case of an overdose with serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it for other infections unless directed by your doctor. While using tigecycline, your doctor may order lab tests (e.g., liver function, fibrinogen levels, blood counts, cultures) to monitor your progress. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. For storage, follow the product instructions or consult your pharmacist. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard expired or unused medication. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about tigecycline. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
